A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

inoculation of a high concentration of PNP with a low inoculum size of C. sp. resulted in a rapid acclimation period, while a low concentration of PNP required a high inoculum size of P. putida to achieve a rapid acclimatization period.
, at low concentrations of the chemical, the inoculum size is critical for the acclimation process, whereas at higher concentrations of the chemical it is not.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the inoculum size is a critical parameter in bioremediation and should be considered when designing a bioremediation strategy.
